pages.c07-p01: Describe what data science is and the stages of the data science cycle
pages.c07-p02: Collect data fairly and describe different types and sources of data
pages.c07-p03: Identify and fix common problems in messy data
pages.c07-p04: Use averages, range and correlation to analyse data, and explain why correlation is not causation
pages.c07-p05: Choose suitable charts for different data and identify misleading visualisations
pages.c07-p06: Present findings as a data story and protect people's privacy when using data

q.q: What is data science?
o: Using data to answer questions and make decisions
q.why: Data science turns data into answers.

q.q: What is data?
q.why: Data needs processing to become information.

q.q: What is the first stage of the data science cycle?
Which stage comes straight after collecting data?
Which stage involves making charts?
Which is the best data question?
o: Do pupils who sleep under 8 hours score lower on Monday quizzes?

q.q: What is big data?
o: Datasets too large or fast for ordinary tools

q.q: The "V" for volume means...
The "V" for variety means...
o: how many different types of data there are

q.q: Which is an example of data science in sport?
o: Analysing passes and shots to choose players

q.q: Which is quantitative data?
Which is qualitative data?
What is primary data?
What is secondary data?
What is open data?
o: Data anyone can use for free

q.q: Which website provides open data about Northern Ireland?
What is a sample?
o: The group you collect data from

q.q: Asking only Year 14 pupils about school lunches would give...
Which survey question is leading?
o: Which meal do you buy most?
How often do you use the canteen?
How would you rate the canteen food from 1 to 5?
Don't you agree the canteen food is great?

q.q: Why include an "Other" option in a survey?
o: So everyone has an answer that fits

q.q: What should you check about secondary data?
o: Who collected it, when and how

q.q: What is data cleaning?
o: Finding and fixing problems in data

q.q: "Y8", "Year 8" and "8" in one column is an example of...
What is a duplicate?
o: An extra copy of the same record

q.q: What is a missing value?
o: A blank where data should be

q.q: An age of 250 in a survey is...
o: an impossible value, probably a typo

q.q: What is an outlier?
o: A value very different from the rest

q.q: Should you always delete outliers?
o: No: check whether they're mistakes or real first

q.q: Why keep a cleaning log?
o: To record every change you made

q.q: Which spreadsheet tool helps fix typos in many cells?
q.why: Find and replace fixes repeated errors.

q.q: How can validation reduce dirty data?
o: It checks data as it's entered

q.q: Which is a good validation for "year group"?
What does "garbage in, garbage out" mean?
q.why: Analysis is only as good as the data.

q.q: How do you calculate the mean?
o: Add all values and divide by how many there are

q.q: What is the median?
o: The middle value when in order

q.q: What is the mode?
What is the range?
What is the mean of 2, 4, 6, 8?
What is the median of 1, 3, 9, 10, 12?
What is the mode of 4, 7, 7, 9, 2?
What is the range of 12, 5, 30, 18?
Which average is best when there's a big outlier?
q.why: The median isn't pulled by outliers.

q.q: What is correlation?
o: Proof that one thing causes another

q.q: As screen time before bed increases, sleep decreases. This is...
q.why: One goes up, the other down.

q.q: Shoe size and quiz score show no pattern. This is...
Ice-cream sales and sunburn rise together because of...
o: a third factor: hot sunny weather

q.q: What is causation?
How can scientists show causation?
o: A fair experiment changing one thing at a time

q.q: Which chart shows correlation best?
What is data visualisation?
o: Showing data as a picture such as a chart

q.q: Which chart is best for comparing categories?
Which chart is best for change over time?
When is a pie chart suitable?
o: Showing parts of a whole with a few categories

q.q: What should the slices of a pie chart add up to?
Which is a misleading chart trick?
o: Starting the y-axis well above zero

q.q: What is cherry-picking data?
o: Showing only data that supports your story

q.q: Why can 3D effects mislead?
o: They can make some parts look bigger than they are

q.q: What should every good chart have?
o: A title and labelled axes with units

q.q: An axis is...
o: a reference line on a chart
q.why: Charts have x and y axes.

q.q: Which chart would best show air quality around Fermanagh?
o: A scatter graph of two people

q.q: Bars of 96 and 98 look very different. What's likely?
o: The y-axis doesn't start at zero

q.q: What is a data story?
o: An explanation of what data shows, why it matters and what to do

q.q: What should a data story start with?
o: The question and the headline finding

q.q: What is a dashboard?
o: A screen showing key charts and numbers together

q.q: Who might use a dashboard?
What is personal data?
o: Information that could identify a living person
q.why: Names, addresses and IDs are personal data.

q.q: What does anonymise mean?
o: Remove details that could identify people

q.q: Why might removing names not anonymise data?
o: Other details in small groups can still identify people

q.q: Which law controls personal data in the UK?
o: UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018

q.q: Under UK GDPR, organisations should...
o: collect only the data they need

q.q: Under UK GDPR, people have the right to...
o: see the data held about them
q.why: Subject access is a key right.

q.q: How can you protect a pupil from being identified in a chart?
o: Combine small groups into larger ones

q.q: What should a data story finish with?
Why give context in a data story?
o: So people know how much data there was and any limits

q.q: Which is NOT personal data?
Which is an example of a data visualisation?
A school wants to know if a new bus route is needed. What data would help most?
o: Where pupils live and how they travel now
q.why: Choose data that answers the question.

q.q: What's wrong with collecting data on "pupils' favourite subject" by asking only the art club?
Why should survey answers use drop-downs where possible?
o: To keep responses consistent and easier to clean

q.q: Which average describes a typical salary best when a few people earn millions?
A study links eating breakfast to higher grades. What should you ask?
A chart about recycling shows only the three best months. This is...
Which is the most honest choice for a bar chart's y-axis?
o: Start it at the smallest value

q.q: Which part of the data science cycle often takes the most time?
What makes data "open"?
o: It's published with permission for anyone to use
It's in a public library book

q.q: Which is a benefit of secondary data?
o: It always fits your question exactly
It is always up to date
It's quick to get and can cover huge numbers of people

q.q: Which is a drawback of primary data?
o: It takes time and effort to collect

q.q: Why might a council publish open data?
o: So people and businesses can use it to make improvements

q.q: What is the mean of 10, 20, 30, 40, 50?
Which of these is quantitative?
What is the purpose of the "communicate" stage?
o: Share findings so people can act on them

q.q: A dashboard for a sports team might show...
o: players' distance run and heart rate

q.q: Which chart would you use to show the percentage of pupils travelling by each method?
q.why: Parts of a whole or category comparisons.

q.q: A sensor records river levels every 10 minutes. This is an example of data with high...
Which is the best reason to check an outlier rather than delete it?
o: It could be real and important
q.why: Real outliers can be key findings.

q.q: Which helps make survey data fair?
o: A large sample from every group

q.q: What is the median of 4, 8, 15, 16?
q.why: With an even count, average the middle two: (8 + 15) ÷ 2 = 11.5.

q.q: A line graph's x-axis jumps from 2015 to 2020 to 2021 with equal gaps. What's wrong?
o: It should be a pie chart

q.q: Which is a privacy-friendly way to share survey results?
o: Show totals for groups, not individual answers
Publish every pupil's name and answer
